jarvis_use: Pre-build classifier for any new Jarvis routine.

name: Variable-pass retrieval exception
summary: Even with a fixed order, use an agent when the number of knowledge-base searches varies per case, so it can do 0..N passes.
jarvis_use: The operator loop already decides how many searches to run; the repetition brake caps it.
steps: If yes, agent decides with a cap

name: Stay interactive if you edit every run
summary: If output needs revision every time, keep it interactive; automate only once output is stable.
jarvis_use: Jarvis works interactively per line; taste-heavy tasks stay with Evens in the loop.

name: Overkill check before building a trigger
summary: Before automating, compare to doing it manually; build a trigger only for real cadence.
jarvis_use: Jarvis defaults to doing the task directly and asks before creating any scheduler.

name: Native tool before custom workflow round-trip
summary: For common actions use a built-in platform tool; reserve custom n8n round-trips for custom work.
jarvis_use: Prefer built-in tools/MCP over custom workflows; no explicit preference order today.
steps: Use it if it covers the action

name: Partial agent coverage
summary: Ask what share of a process an agent can do, always route that share to the agent, keep trust-heavy steps with humans.
jarvis_use: Jarvis does its part and holds sends/pay/delete and login walls for Evens via ask_owner.
steps: Route that share to the agent

name: Pin model and effort for scheduled jobs
summary: An automation defaulted to an older model and ran slowly; set model and reasoning explicitly and avoid usage-heavy fast modes.
jarvis_use: Jev picks per job; scheduled jobs should store their pinned tier.

name: Re-tune tier thresholds when limits change
summary: When provider session limits grow, relax aggressive downgrading where quality matters, but keep context hygiene.
jarvis_use: Jev thresholds reviewed when provider limits change.

name: Per-workspace engine selection
summary: Sibling folders, one with a provider-routing settings.local.json and one without; the launch directory chooses the engine so experiments don't leak into the main setup.
jarvis_use: Pin Jev routes per workspace config instead of global settings.
steps: Launch from the folder for the wanted engine

name: Choose retrieval by what a human would do
summary: Filter for known fields and small subsets, SQL for totals/rankings/trends, full context for summaries and ordered content, vector search for a local answer in a large corpus.
jarvis_use: Jev classify step that picks the retrieval method per question.
steps: Ask what a careful human would do
Map to filter / SQL / full / vector

name: Persona debate panel for decisions
summary: 3-7 personas research independently and debate, optionally to consensus; the human reads the debate. Consensus mode can run away on tokens; usage figures are claims.
jarvis_use: Capped cheap-tier debate for hard choices; Evens gets the transcript, not a decision.

name: One lane / one ship per session
summary: Classify the session path before acting, work one system per session, and have the principal pick at most one ship.
jarvis_use: Jarvis classifies each request into one lane and asks before adding a second deliverable.
steps: Ask Evens to pick at most one ship

name: Pain-first tool adoption (weight-off-shoulders filter)
summary: Learn what a new tool does, but adopt it only if it removes a real current pain; viral is not a reason.
jarvis_use: Score new tools/signals against BUS300 before proposing; depends on signal ingestion, which is missing.
steps: Ask if the release removes it

name: Productivity-dip rule for stack switches
summary: Every switch costs a temporary dip; switch only if the end-state line ends above the current trajectory. The 20% figure is the speaker's estimate.
jarvis_use: Jarvis states the expected dip and end state when proposing a migration; Evens decides.
steps: Switch only if it ends higher

name: Kill on opportunity cost
summary: An opportunity is good or bad only relative to the cost of pursuing it versus the main line of work.
jarvis_use: Jarvis frames side ideas against BUS300; keep/kill is Evens's call.

name: Use NL builders for linear workflows only
summary: A natural-language workflow builder handled linear paths but produced broken orchestrator/sub-agent systems.
jarvis_use: Only relevant if Jarvis generates n8n workflows; label linear vs agentic first.

name: Tier selection by cost and capability
summary: Small tier for cheap bulk work, mid tier as default, frontier for hard reasoning (keep under about 20%); output tokens cost more than input.
jarvis_use: Jev already routes small/mid/frontier; cap frontier share and watch output-heavy jobs.
steps: Send bulk reading and formatting to small tier
Reserve frontier for planning and hard reasoning

name: Per-step model routing (planner, reasoner, stylist)
summary: Split a job into steps and route each to the cheapest model that fits: a small model plans or summarizes into structured fields, a reasoning model writes content, a strong writer model turns it into HTML.
jarvis_use: Jev picks a tier per job today; extend it to route individual steps within a job to different models.
steps: Identify plan, think and format steps
Route plan/format to cheap tier with structured output fields
Route think step to reasoning model
Pass step output as next step's input

name: Choose model per sub-agent
summary: Set gather or search sub-agents to cheaper models and keep frontier for synthesis.
jarvis_use: Blocked on sub-agents, which Jarvis lacks; once sub-agents exist, Jev assigns tiers per sub-agent.
steps: Decide sub-agent model by task difficulty
Use cheap tiers for gather agents

name: Cheap or local models wrapped as skills
summary: Wrap a call to a cheaper or local model in a skill the main session can invoke.
jarvis_use: Needs a skills library loader; then expose Jev cheap tiers as callable skills.
steps: Create a skill that calls the cheaper/local model

name: Cap effort at high; change model instead of effort
summary: Keep reasoning effort at high by default; higher modes overthink and over-delegate at more cost. Switch models for cost/quality trade-offs and check cost-vs-score curves before raising effort.
jarvis_use: Make 'effort = high, escalate model not effort' an explicit Jev default and log when effort is raised.
steps: Compare outcome vs cost when testing higher effort

name: Same-prompt, same-harness model bakeoff with cost/time/token ledger
summary: Run the identical prompt on the same codebase and harness with each model (including cheap vs frontier one-shot design prompts); record cost, wall time and tokens, compare outputs, and ask whether the pricier model is worth its price multiple.
jarvis_use: Per-job cost meter exists; missing is a same-task cross-model ledger that grounds Jev routing in Jarvis's own runs.
steps: Run each model on identical inputs
Compare outputs plus ledger; judge price multiple

name: Compare outputs by the wrapper, not just the model
summary: Same model gives very different results depending on harness, skills, hooks, MCP, memory and docs; record the environment with every comparison and fix the harness before swapping models.
jarvis_use: Ledger rows record harness version and context used alongside model results.
steps: Hold the wrapper fixed or note differences
Invest in wrapper before switching models

name: Golden-task replay on a new model; default first, swap after eval
summary: On a new release, run your regular workflows unchanged on it before routing real work; start with a default model and swap only after an evaluation shows it is better for that use case.
jarvis_use: A fixed set of Jarvis golden tasks replayed before Jev adds a model to any pool.
steps: Pick regular workflows as golden tasks
Run unchanged on the new model
Note interpretation, stopping and verification differences

name: Open-ended creative probe
summary: Give a new model an open creative goal (build anything as an HTML document) to see its taste, range and time.
jarvis_use: Low-stakes probe before routing creative jobs to a new model.
steps: Run same prompt on another model

name: Harness-free diagram test with render-and-check
summary: Ask models in plain chat for Excalidraw JSON, render and compare; without verification, errors like clipped text show up.
jarvis_use: Jarvis can screenshot; missing is a mandatory render-and-check step before delivering diagrams (independent verifier).
steps: Note errors a check would catch

name: Primary plus cross-provider fallback model
summary: Configure a main model and a fallback; a fallback on the same vendor via a different gateway fails together, so pick a different provider. Short-term memory keyed by channel/chat id lets the agent reuse recent object ids.
jarvis_use: Jev has escalation across vendors but no defined per-route outage fallback; idle session continuation covers chat memory.
steps: Configure fallback on a different provider

name: Fall back to previous model version when new one degrades
summary: Keep the earlier model version available and use it where it performs better on your tasks.
jarvis_use: Jev keeps the prior version as a route option per task type, decided by ledger results.
steps: Compare new vs previous on own tasks

name: Model-agnostic harness and open-weights hedge
summary: Model is the engine, harness the car, human the driver. Hosted closed models can be withdrawn, so keep procedures, memory and data model-agnostic, know an open-weights alternative (hosted if too big for local), and invest in owned processes and hardware.
jarvis_use: Jarvis's procedural memory is model-independent and Jev spans several vendors; missing is a tested open-weights fallback route.
steps: List closed models the workflow depends on
Use a hosted runner if too big for local

name: Closed vs local model compute tradeoff
summary: Hosted models perform well partly due to provider compute; local or VPS models need enough RAM/VRAM to run fast.
jarvis_use: Jev checks Mac RAM/VRAM and the resource floor before any local-model route.
steps: Use hosted when local compute is too small

name: One gateway credential for many models
summary: Create one router key (OpenRouter) stored once as a credential and reuse it across nodes and agent chat models; pick the model per step; unified billing and usage. Native nodes only when they offer a needed modality (e.g. Gemini document analysis).
jarvis_use: Jev already spans vendor pools via env-var-referenced credentials; key creation stays with Evens.

name: Route around a native-integration bug via the router
summary: When a new model errors on a native node (bad parameter values) but the older model works, isolate it, then call the same model through the router.
jarvis_use: Jarvis isolates by testing the prior model and reports; alternate routes go through Jev, never ad-hoc key swaps (rule 6).
steps: Test older model on same integration

name: Read real provider limits at call time
summary: Context window and price can differ between a router listing and the vendor console; check actual limits.
jarvis_use: Jev stores per-route context/price as read from the provider, tagged with a check date.
steps: Compare price and context window vs vendor

name: Native-only provider features
summary: Some features (OpenAI Responses built-in tools) are not available through aggregators; use the native credential when needed.
jarvis_use: Jev's routing table notes which features exist only on native APIs.
steps: If built-in tools needed, use native credential

name: Provider built-in web/file search with context size, location and domain limits
summary: Enable the Responses API so the model itself does web or file search with citations; options for search context size, location targeting and an allowed-domains list.
jarvis_use: Jarvis has its own web_search/fetch; add allowed-domain restriction for domain-specific lookups.
steps: Set context size, location, allowed domains

name: Try a newer same-family model before declaring a feature broken
summary: The allowed-domains filter failed on GPT-4.1 but worked on GPT-5 mini.
jarvis_use: On a provider feature error, Jarvis retries on a newer model in the same family before reporting it broken.

name: Responses API extra options (cache key, metadata, service tier)
summary: Saved prompt id, service tier, safety id, conversation id, prompt cache key, metadata tags, logprobs.
jarvis_use: Jarvis has prompt cache; add metadata tags per job for traceability; keep memory local, not vendor conversation ids.
steps: Set prompt cache key and metadata

name: Subscription inference via Codex OAuth device code
summary: Pick OpenAI Codex as provider, sign in through the device-code flow, and use a ChatGPT subscription instead of metered API keys.
jarvis_use: Jev could include subscription-backed routes where allowed; login is done by Evens.
steps: Open auth URL and sign in

name: Aggregator gateway for media generation
summary: Access many image/video models (Veo, Sora, Nano Banana, GPT Image) through one aggregator (Kie.ai, FAL.ai); prototype in the provider playground, copy the HTTP request, use fast variants to cut cost, split create vs edit models.
jarvis_use: If built, one gated media gateway; every paid generation needs a quote and Evens's per-job OK (media-gen-cost-gate); ArtCraft stays default.
steps: Pick fast variant when good enough

name: Classify video-model jobs: offline diffusion vs real-time autoregressive
summary: Decide whether a job needs an offline coherent clip (diffusion; capped length, extend from last frame) or real-time steerable output (autoregressive next-frame world model).
jarvis_use: Jarvis routes video requests to offline plates and never promises an interactive world model.
steps: Ask if mid-shot input or unlimited length is needed
If no, diffusion clip; extend from last frame

name: Camera-pose and promptable-event control of a world model
summary: Speculative: stream phone camera pose and text events into a world model and record output.
jarvis_use: Research watch item only.

name: Voice LLM chosen on latency and cost
summary: Premium voices and smarter LLMs add latency; each model shows its own cost and ms; compare on live test calls (localhost felt slower than deployed), listen for slowness and repeated filler, and pick a model tested for instruction following.
jarvis_use: Jev routes voice turns to a fast-enough tier; missing is real-surface latency measurement and recorded A/B before swaps (BUS300-adjacent; live :4018 changes need Evens).
steps: Run same test call per model on the real surface
Listen for slowness and repeated filler

name: Iterate system prompts as a diff, then test
summary: Generate a prompt edit, review struck and added text, accept/refine/discard, then test by talking to the agent; repeat.
jarvis_use: Jarvis prompt edits are shown as diffs and adopted only after a test run.

name: Context dumb-zone handoff before quality decays
summary: Large windows are a false ceiling; models degrade well before the limit and lost-in-the-middle worsens. Track context and hand off to a fresh session before the threshold instead of compacting.
jarvis_use: Jarvis keeps lean context (last 3 screenshots); add a per-model token budget that writes a handoff and continues fresh, which also serves resume-after-reboot.
steps: Near threshold, write handoff and start fresh
Do not rely on mid-conversation details

name: Give the why (intent, audience, purpose)
summary: State the bigger task, who it is for, what they need and why each constraint exists (e.g. it is my writing style); this improves instruction following and steers retrieval to the right context files. Scope strong models ambitiously.
jarvis_use: Jarvis task cards and sub-model calls carry a one-line goal, audience and why.

name: Tell it what to do, not what not to do
summary: Rewrite negative instructions as positive targets; keep a don't only with context.
jarvis_use: Jarvis phrases model instructions as positive specs; variant that differs from the don't-list method below.
steps: Keep a don't only with its reason

name: Negative prompting with a do-not-act gate
summary: Brief like an intern: for questions the deliverable is an assessment; report and stop; don't fix, send, edit or delete until told to go; do the simplest thing that works.
jarvis_use: Jarvis already holds send/pay/delete for Evens's OK with ask-then-resume.

name: Say less, not more
summary: With a capable model and good environment, a short steer plus the why beats numbered rule lists; standing behavior lives in system, memory and skill files.
jarvis_use: Trim per-turn instructions; depends on a skills library to hold detail.
steps: Replace rule lists with a short steer

name: No standing 'explain your reasoning' line
summary: On one model a standing reveal-reasoning instruction can trigger refusals; ask for conclusions plus evidence instead.
jarvis_use: Audit Jarvis system prompts for reveal-chain-of-thought lines.

name: Observable-behavior specs instead of vague adjectives
summary: Turn vague instructions ('off brand', 'more charismatic') into observable black-and-white behaviors and use them as prompts and checks.
jarvis_use: Jarvis asks Evens to turn vague feedback into concrete checks and stores them as testable criteria for a verifier.

name: Ask to explain or test, not for an opinion
summary: Opinion questions invite sycophancy; ask the model to explain how something works or test the claim against data.
jarvis_use: Jarvis converts 'does this look right?' into a concrete check; needs an independent verifier to be reliable.

name: Treat vendor benchmarks and launch posts as claims
summary: Pick benchmarks matched to the job (long-horizon agentic, screen understanding, multi-step function calling) and re-test on your own tasks; read launch posts for access, dated plan windows and price multiples, which hint at capability differences.
jarvis_use: Jarvis writes a short access/price/window note per new model with numbers tagged UNVERIFIED until its own eval or the vendor page confirms.

name: Price tier as a capability tell
summary: A model priced like a given tier should be benchmarked against same-priced peers; version numbering is another tell.
jarvis_use: Benchmark a new model against the same-price model already in Jev's table.

name: Classify a 'frontier killer' as base model vs orchestrator
summary: Determine whether a release is a new LLM or a conductor routing to existing models; treat orchestrator benchmark wins as mixture results.
jarvis_use: Tag model announcements as base vs router before any routing-table change.
steps: Ask: new base model or multi-agent?
Treat orchestrator wins as mixture results

name: Fusion (broadcast + judge) vs split-and-delegate
summary: Send one prompt to several models with a judge merging, or split the task and delegate parts to specialists; both add perspective at a cost in speed and money.
jarvis_use: Jev could pick broadcast+judge for high-stakes single answers and split-delegate (needs sub-agents) for multi-part tasks, with cost noted.
steps: Fusion: broadcast to N models, judge merges
Weigh perspective vs latency and cost

name: Managed file search instead of a custom RAG pipeline (claim)
summary: Drop docs into a managed file-search store for embeddings and chat instead of building chunk/embed/vector pipelines; the cost claim is unexplained.
jarvis_use: Candidate for low-stakes doc Q&A only after cost and quality are verified.

name: Diagnose method vs compute vs data
summary: Neural nets stalled for lack of hardware and labeled data, not method; identify which blocks progress before rewriting.
jarvis_use: When a Jarvis capability fails, classify the blocker as method, compute or data first.

name: Give the goal, not micro-steps (AlexNet lesson)
summary: Let the system learn the approach from full data and objective rather than prescribing intermediate features; measure on a shared benchmark.
jarvis_use: Give Jarvis goal plus context and verify the result instead of micro-instructions.

name: Backpropagation as a post-mortem analogy
summary: Trace error backward and assign blame to each step in proportion to its contribution before changing anything.
jarvis_use: Procedural memory post-mortems attribute a failed run to the steps that caused it.

name: Perceptron and transformer history (background)
summary: Perceptron learned weights from examples (1958); transformers read sequences in parallel and next-token pretraining led to GPT and ChatGPT.
jarvis_use: Background knowledge only.
steps: Parallel attention plus next-token pretraining at scale

Add desktop apps, paid software, bookmarks, open tabs/history (Safari tabs with Evens's permission)
Map each category to the tool(s) where it lives
Connect and prove one at a time, tier-1 first

steps: Else store the key once as a named credential or env var
Owner creates/pastes keys and completes OAuth
Broken connector: report for re-auth, do not route around

summary: Create a dedicated key per agent/connector scoped to only the resource needed; deny edit/delete/team actions.
steps: Create a dedicated key for the agent
Scope to read only the needed resource

Keep integrations as scripts/recipes in the folder
Use desktop connectors knowing they won't carry over

Ask the agent to install it (or click add)
Apply the repo install gate (license, archived, pin)

steps: Copy the remote MCP URL from the vendor's MCP page
Add custom connector, name it, paste URL
Surface the full OAuth link to Evens and wait
Verify connector is on before prompting dependent work

steps: If none, wrap the API into a CLI
Use MCP only when nothing else works

Agent calls the CLI through shell

Ask it to turn it into a CLI with keys from env

Keep CLI > API > skills > MCP order

Test and save as a recipe/skill
